problems.stem: A peer review of a classmate's prototype reads in full: 'Great work, very clear and professional. 5/5.' Why does this fall short of scholarly critique?
options: It is too short to be polite.
It is praise with a rating but names no specific element, problem, or criterion the author can act on.
It should not include a numeric rating.
problems.explanation: Scholarly critique identifies a specific element, the problem with it, and the criterion behind the judgment; encouragement alone is not critique.

problems.stem: Which peer comment gives the author the most actionable, defensible feedback?
options: I would have picked a different color scheme; blue feels nicer to me.
The Module 2 objective says 'evaluate,' but the matching activity only asks learners to recall definitions, so the assessment is misaligned.
This is not really my style.
I think most people would prefer a video here.
problems.explanation: Tying critique to a shared criterion (objective-to-assessment alignment) lets the author judge the point on its merits, unlike a preference statement.

problems.stem: You ask an AI to draft a critique of a peer's storyboard and it lists a 'missing accessibility statement' the storyboard does not actually have a place for. What is the correct move before submitting?
options: Submit the AI critique as written; it sounds thorough.
Verify each flagged issue against the peer's actual artifact and remove or correct points that are not real.
Add even more AI-generated points to look rigorous.
Tell the peer the AI found the problems, so they are not your responsibility.
problems.explanation: An unverified AI critique can fabricate issues; you must confirm each point against the real artifact before it becomes your review.

problems.stem: You received eight peer comments. A reviewer says your response 'shows no judgment' because you applied all eight edits without comment. What practice fixes this?
options: Apply none of the comments instead.
Record a disposition for each comment, accept, modify, or reject, with a one-line reason.
Ask the peers to rewrite their comments.
Only respond to the comments from the highest-rated peer.
problems.explanation: Logging a reasoned accept, modify, or reject per comment shows that peer review informed your judgment rather than replacing it.
